classification.difficultyReason: Recognise perpendicular flight legs, calculate the resultant direction using a right triangle, then reverse the bearing.

content.prompt: An aeroplane flies on a bearing of $060^\circ\mathrm{T}$ for $80\text{ km}$ and then on a bearing of $150^\circ\mathrm{T}$ for $70\text{ km}$. What is the bearing of the starting point from the final position of the aeroplane? Calculate your answer to one decimal place.

answer.short:
$281.2^\circ\mathrm{T}$

Use the right triangle formed by the flight legs, then reverse the bearing.
answer.worked:
Let $A$ be the starting point, $B$ the turning point and $C$ the final position. The bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $240^\circ\mathrm{T}$, so $\angle ABC=240^\circ-150^\circ=90^\circ$.

Let $\alpha=\angle BAC$.

$$\begin{align*}\tan\alpha&=\frac{70}{80}\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{70}{80}\right)\end{align*}$$

The direction $AC$ is clockwise from $AB$. Hence the bearing of $C$ from $A$ is $60^\circ+\alpha$. Reverse this bearing to find the bearing of $A$ from $C$:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Bearing}&=60^\circ+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{70}{80}\right)+180^\circ\\\text{Bearing}&\approx281.2^\circ\mathrm{T}\end{align*}$$
